problem: Solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDE for diffusion models is computationally slow and sensitive to hyperparameter tuning, limiting practical high-dimensional sampling.
approach: Introduce a functional tensor train (FTT) solver that exploits low-rank structures for efficient PDE approximation, combined with a backward-in-time iterative scheme from backward stochastic differential equations.
contribution: A fast, robust diffusion sampling method that enables high-fidelity sampling from challenging target distributions with improved computational efficiency.

problem: Existing differentially private code generation assumes prompts are public while protecting only code, failing to protect sensitive information in both prompts and code.
approach: Propose PrivCode++ with a two-stage DP framework using Privacy-Free Latent Conditioning to enable fine-tuning without direct access to sensitive prompts or code snippets.
contribution: First work on DP code generation protecting both prompts and code, achieving substantially higher utility than baselines with stronger privacy guarantees.

problem: Data mixture selection for large language models is costly to search and existing scaling laws fail to extrapolate to large model sizes.
approach: Propose CAMEL, a capacity-aware mixture law modeling validation loss with nonlinear interactions between model size and data mixture, plus a loss-to-benchmark prediction law.
contribution: Reduce mixture optimization costs by 50% while improving downstream benchmark performance by up to 3% when applied to Mixture-of-Experts models up to 55B-A1.2B parameters.

problem: Applying machine learning to solve long-standing mathematical conjectures faces extreme reward sparsity, making standard RL ineffective.
approach: Recast counterexample construction as sparse-reward RL on graphs using constrained options-based HRL with equivariant graph neural network policies.
contribution: First application of hierarchical RL to commutative algebra, consistently outperforming classical RL and greedy search on Kalai's algebraic Hirsch conjecture.

problem: Mixture-of-Experts models exhibit imbalanced routing that causes compute and memory failures on overloaded devices during post-training and inference.
approach: Introduce Least-Loaded Expert Parallelism (LLEP), an algorithm that dynamically reroutes excess tokens from overloaded to underutilized devices while respecting memory constraints.
contribution: Achieve up to 5x speedup and 4x peak memory reduction with ~1.9x faster inference for gpt-oss-120b compared to standard expert parallelism.

problem: Spectral representation alignment benefits diffusion training but the mechanism remains unclear, limiting principled improvements to diffusion models.
approach: Investigate connections between self-supervised spectral representation learning and diffusion through shared perturbation kernels, proposing spectral representation alignment regularization.
contribution: Consistent generation quality gains across images and 3D point clouds by integrating spectral regularization into diffusion training objectives.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs requires balancing data privacy and model IP protection, but existing methods protect only one or compromise utility.
approach: Propose PISA with three methods: Manifold Rectification Pre-training for robustness, Dual-Stream Semantic Compensation for feature recovery, and Utility-Aware Gradient Rectification.
contribution: Achieve 23% performance gain over privacy-prioritized baseline on GLUE while simultaneously protecting both data privacy and model intellectual property.

problem: Standard SSL for automatic modulation recognition struggles with ineffective augmentations, spectral instability, and semantic drift.
approach: Introduce Dynamic-Consistency Contrastive Learning (DyCo-CL) coupling Virtual Adversarial Augmentation with semantic consistency loss and Signal-Adaptive Swin Backbone.
contribution: Achieve 6.27% accuracy gain in 1-shot modulation recognition settings over prior methods.

problem: Group counterfactual explanations either don't generalize to new members, require strong assumptions, or poorly preserve group geometry.
approach: Learn an explicit optimal transport map sending any group instance to its counterfactual, minimizing total transport cost without re-optimization.
contribution: Enable generalization with fewer parameters, preserve group geometry, and provide mathematical characterization of group counterfactuals for linear classifiers.

problem: Efficient expansion of strategy sets in PSRO can lead to inefficient population growth that poorly approximates the full game.
approach: Guide population expansion by directly minimizing Population Exploitability (PE) through a two-phase exploration-selection framework with parameter-sharing conditional neural networks.
contribution: Achieve lower exploitability and better Nash equilibrium approximation with significantly fewer policy iterations than prior PSRO methods across multiple games.

problem: Composing multiple constraints in guided diffusion/flow model sampling causes off-manifold drift that degrades generation fidelity.
approach: Identify gradient misalignment as root cause and propose Conflict-Aware Additive Guidance (g^CAR), a learnable method that dynamically detects and resolves gradient conflicts.
contribution: Effectively rectify off-manifold drift in composite constrained generation across synthetic data, image editing, and planning tasks.

problem: Large models are costly to deploy across different computational budgets, requiring separate training for each budget.
approach: Leverage low-rank weight decomposition with nested, importance-based consolidation to extract submodels of increasing capabilities from a single pretrained model.
contribution: Enable train-once-deploy-everywhere paradigm with graceful cost-performance trade-offs without retraining for each budget.

problem: The duality between structured state-space models and masked attention is limited to scalar-identity cases with unclear generalization potential.
approach: Formalize and extend the Structured State-Space Duality to general diagonal SSMs, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for equivalence to semiseparable masked attention.
contribution: Diagonal SSMs match scalar case complexity while supporting richer dynamics; clarify that standard softmax attention's rank explosion prevents duality extension.

problem: Current coding benchmarks lack exceptionally challenging problems, have insufficient test coverage, and depend on online APIs limiting accessibility.
approach: Introduce LiveOIBench featuring 403 expert-curated problems from 72 Informatics Olympiad contests with an average of 60 test cases each and offline evaluation.
contribution: Enable direct comparison of 34 LLMs to elite human contestants, finding GPT-5 achieves 81.76th percentile while GPT-OSS-120B reaches 60th percentile.

problem: Existing HGR maximal correlation methods have prohibitive computational cost for high-dimensional multimodal learning.
approach: Replace explicit whitening with centered l2-normalized cosine alignment in local-batch Gram space and remove invariant self-correlation via Trivial Spectrum Suppression.
contribution: Consistent gains across retrieval, classification, and emotion recognition with O(m^2K) structural cost and stable behavior at extreme feature dimensions.

problem: Detecting long-context attention heads in LLMs requires expensive inference on actual long texts without analyzing inherent parameter properties.
approach: Use kernel methods to analyze frequency kernels of attention heads and design Long-context Potential Score (LPS) to measure inherent long-context processing potential.
contribution: Fully static and offline LPS metrics predict long-context capability better than inference-based methods; amplifying low-frequency kernels improves long-context performance.

problem: Post-training flow matching models for alignment requires preference optimization but involves expensive preference collection and reward modeling.
approach: Propose Flow Matching Adversarial Imitation Learning (FAIL) minimizing policy-expert divergence through adversarial training with pathwise gradient variants.
contribution: Fine-tune FLUX with only 13K demonstrations achieving competitive prompt-following and aesthetic performance while generalizing to discrete generation.

problem: Model extraction attacks enable adversaries to replicate proprietary DNN functionality, but verifying ownership with rigorous guarantees is challenging.
approach: Employ mutual information to quantify model similarity, propose a practical verification threshold, and provide theoretical guarantees for certified ownership verification.
contribution: State-of-the-art certified ownership verification against model extraction attacks across multiple datasets and domains.

problem: Language models memorize and reproduce verbatim spans from training data, raising copyright and compliance risks.
approach: Propose Anchored Decoding, keeping generation bounded to a permissively trained safe LM while adaptively allocating information budget and enforcing per-step constraints.
contribution: Preserve near-original fluency while eliminating up to 75% of measurable copying gap between risky and safe models with modest inference overhead.

problem: Scaling RL for LLMs faces vanishing learning signals when problem difficulty distributions are static relative to model capabilities.
approach: Introduce RLVE with 400 procedurally generated verifiable environments that dynamically adapt problem difficulty during training.
contribution: Achieve 3.37% absolute average improvement across six reasoning benchmarks with environment scaling, substantially outperforming continued original RL training.

problem: Attribution methods produce unspecific explanations highlighting both important and irrelevant features.
approach: Show that using logits as attribution target is problematic; propose using distributions of attributions over multiple classes with existing methods.
contribution: Improve attribution specificity of 18 methods across 7 architectures up to 2x on common benchmarks via multi-class distribution analysis.

problem: Neural PDE solvers struggle to scale to industrial-grade meshes with over 10^8 cells due to prohibitive GPU memory requirements.
approach: Introduce Transolver-3 with faster slice/deslice operations using matrix multiplication properties, geometry slice tiling, amortized training, and physical state caching.
contribution: Handle meshes with over 160 million cells achieving impressive performance on aircraft and automotive design simulation tasks.

problem: Latent-space visual reasoning lacks sufficient semantic richness and visual supervision limits diverse region-level reasoning tasks.
approach: Propose SLVR with two-stage framework: enrich latents with attribute-level supervision, then align across multiple queries using Multi-query Group Relative Policy Optimization.
contribution: Improve robustness and semantic consistency of latent visual reasoning over baselines; introduce SLV-Set with 400K region annotations and SV-QA benchmark.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models suffer from information collapse where language instructions become predictable from vision alone, causing models to ignore language.
approach: Propose LangForce enforcing instruction following via Bayesian decomposition with learnable Latent Action Queries to maximize Pointwise Mutual Information between actions and language.
contribution: Achieve 11.3% improvement on challenging OOD SimplerEnv benchmark, validating robust language grounding in robotic manipulation.

problem: Large vision-language models hallucinate by relying on language priors without visual grounding.
approach: Propose Dynamic Entropy-Guided Attention Perturbation (DEGAP) that perturbs visual attention layer-wise and dynamically selects layers based on model confidence.
contribution: Effectively mitigate various hallucination types across seven benchmarks while maintaining strong general VQA performance.

problem: The relationship between fixed-budget and fixed-confidence best-arm identification remains unclear despite matching sample complexities for K-armed bandits.
approach: Propose FC2FB meta-algorithm converting fixed-confidence algorithms to fixed-budget by leveraging existing FC methods constructively.
contribution: Show that fixed-budget is no harder than fixed-confidence up to logarithmic factors with improved sample complexity for several FB problems.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs for robotic planning requires costly chain-of-thought supervision and manual reward engineering for reinforcement learning.
approach: Propose Self-CriTeach where LLMs autonomously generate symbolic planning domains serving dual roles: generating problem-plan pairs for SFT and structured reward functions.
contribution: Achieve higher planning success, stronger cross-task generalization, reduced inference cost, and resistance to imperfect logical states.

problem: Multi-LLM serving on shared GPUs degrades inference performance, particularly time-to-first-token, due to lack of future workload awareness.
approach: Propose one-for-many GPU prewarming loading multiple model parameters based on workload forecasts, with model placement optimization and KV cache reservation.
contribution: Reduce tail time-to-first-token by up to 50.8x compared to autoscaling while supporting 2.5x higher throughput than GPU-sharing systems.

problem: Amortised sampling methods and particle-based methods each have limitations when sampling from unnormalised densities.
approach: Connect sequential Monte Carlo and neural sequential samplers via maximum-entropy RL, using learned samplers as SMC proposals with adaptive weight tempering.
contribution: Demonstrate improvements in approximating true distributions and training stability over both amortised and Monte Carlo methods alone.

problem: Estimating scaling laws requires substantial computational resources with limited guidance on strategic budget allocation.
approach: Explore Successive Halving combined with parametric and non-parametric surrogate models for systematic compute budget allocation.
contribution: Mean relative improvements of up to 5.47% on synthetic datasets while saving up to 98.7% computational cost compared to exhaustive approaches.

problem: Machine unlearning for multimodal LLMs risks hallucinations and rigid responses after unlearning, compromising model usability.
approach: Propose ASRU combining activation steering for initial refusal with reinforcement learning for fine-grained refusal boundaries using customized reward functions.
contribution: Improve unlearning effectiveness (+24.6%) and generation quality (5.8x) while preserving model utility on Qwen3-VL.

problem: Incremental object detection suffers from catastrophic forgetting and increased confusion between old and new classes due to separation-oriented paradigms.
approach: Propose Symbiosis-Inspired Knowledge Distillation leveraging object co-occurrence and occlusion dependencies via Spatial and Semantic Symbiosis Distillation.
contribution: Preserve old class knowledge and stabilize semantic topology during incremental learning over existing class-incremental methods.

problem: Existing load-balancing methods for Mixture-of-Experts are heuristic and operate on noisy mini-batch statistics, introducing bias.
approach: Propose phi-balancing, a principled framework minimizing a convex symmetric differentiable potential of expected routing distribution via mirror descent.
contribution: Consistently outperform prior baselines on pretraining and fine-tuning with more stable and effective expert utilization.

problem: Self-play LLM training exhibits non-sustained improvement where early gains degrade, caused by diversity collapse into recurring patterns.
approach: Propose R-Diverse with Memory-Augmented Penalty to discourage recycling across iterations and Skill-Aware Measurement to evaluate true reasoning diversity.
contribution: Sustain gains over more iterations and consistently outperform prior self-play methods across math and reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Understanding and interpreting LLM activations is difficult with most techniques requiring complex specialized methods.
approach: Train LLMs as Activation Oracles to accept LLM activations as inputs and answer natural language questions about them in generalist settings.
contribution: Recover fine-tuned information without training on fine-tuned activations; match or exceed white-box baselines on downstream interpretability tasks.

problem: Masked diffusion language models for non-autoregressive generation suffer performance loss when unmasking multiple positions in parallel due to ignored interactions.
approach: Propose Dilated Unmasking Scheduler partitioning positions into non-adjacent dilated groups and unmasking in parallel to minimize joint entropy gain.
contribution: Achieve up to 5.8x wall-clock speedup over token-by-token decoding with predictable quality-speed trade-offs.

problem: Block-wise decoding in diffusion language models uses rigid fixed partitioning that fragments semantic constituents, suboptimizing performance.
approach: Propose Swordsman, an entropy-driven adaptive block partitioning framework identifying constituent boundaries via entropy shifts to align with semantic structures.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance via training-free adaptive partitioning and dynamic threshold adjustment for improved efficiency and stability.

problem: Standard deep learning approaches for antibody engineering model marginal sequence distributions and miss affinity maturation as a source of evolutionary information.
approach: Introduce CoSiNE, a continuous-time Markov chain parameterized by neural networks that captures epistatic effects with quadratic error bounds in branch length.
contribution: Outperform language models in zero-shot variant effect prediction; introduce Guided Gillespie for classifier-guided antibody affinity optimization.

problem: Learning optimal reactive policies in non-Markovian environments with hard state aggregation is challenging under existing convergence assumptions.
approach: Introduce Committed Q-learning where behavior policy commits to single action upon entering feature, resampling only when observed feature changes.
contribution: Prove almost-sure convergence to optimal reactive policy under rewire-robustness assumption strictly weaker than q-star-realizability.

problem: Vision-language models produce self-reflective statements like rechecking images but may be learned patterns rather than genuine visual re-examination.
approach: Introduce VISUALSWAP framework replacing images mid-reasoning with visually similar but semantically different ones to test visual re-examination.
contribution: Reveal that VLMs overwhelmingly miss swaps (accuracy drops 60%); thinking models are 3x more vulnerable; multi-turn user instructions restore grounding.
